review.title: the review page
redlines: The design laid the panel beside a plain card; the build lays both on a ruled, tilted desk (panel.desk) and scales the frame to fit, with the zoom read out in the corner (panel.zoom).

The design's tabs were Blueprints / Rules / Screens. Built: Blueprints / Rules / Threads with counts, and the screens moved into the bar as a picker (panel.screen-picker) that names the page in the frame.

Rules are grouped under the screen they are about, with a sticky screen head, tier marks on the left and the ask — sign / asks / fixed / walk — as a coloured badge on the right (ADR 0006 §4). The design had story headings and one sign / walk word.
The bar carries Start walkdown, the viewport presets and Pin mode; Recording as moved to the settings pop-over under the gear.
The footer counts verified rules and opens the Legend on demand; the design printed the legend inline.

The design's bar read Prototype / App whatever was behind them. Built: each side is named for what it shows on the screen in hand — Design or Proposal, App, As-built or Stand-in — and a side with nothing to show is disabled, as is all of it on a page that is no screen (panel.dock.surfaces-say-what-they-show).

rule-detail.title: rule detail
redlines: The design had a verdict block at the top — a why box, Pass and Fail — and a separate Threads list with its own composer at the bottom. Built: one conversation, one composer under it (ADR 0006): the text box above the buttons, Waive alone on the left, Reply / Fail / Pass on the right.
The statement is followed by because and history, then the screen and the steps drawn as given / when / then with anchors as chips (ADR 0004). The design showed statement, evidence, steps, verify.
Evidence, acceptance and the check source sit below the conversation rather than above it.
The steppers (← →) and ← All rules are where the design put them.
The conversation shows only the last thing said; the whole history is one slide to the right, behind History (n-0319). The design showed every thread in place.

rule-detail-since-signed.title: rule detail, a rule you signed has changed since
redlines: The block sits directly above the turn line, as drawn, but the turn line is in the conversation, which the built rule detail puts after the steps and evidence. The design had the conversation above Evidence and Steps (see rule detail's own redlines).
Steps are shown as written: a backtick stays a backtick. The design set prototype: null and its kin as code.
The turn line keeps the words it already had. The design's Pass signs this wording and ends the conversation was written by the design agent and is not asked for by this rule.
Drawn over the example blueprint, where nothing is signed on older words: the signature and the answer are stood in by the capture, so the dates and the changes are illustrative.

thread-panel.title: the thread screen
redlines: The design's composer offered Answer and Waive under the box. Built: the box, then Reply — and on a thread that has ended, the closed banner above it says how it ended and that a fail on the rule reopens it (ADR 0006 §3). Done / Reopen appear only on a thread no walkable rule owns.
The head names the author, the id and the reason (finding, feedback, request…) beside the status chip; the design had id and status alone.
This screen is reached from the Threads tab — which lists only threads no rule can be walked — or from a tag in a rule's conversation. The design reached it from a rule's Threads list.
Day dividers and the NEW line are as designed.
An open question's screen carries its choices under the question, with Answer and Later at the foot, so it is answered here as well as on the rule (n-0319).

settings.title: settings
redlines: The design drew a card: Record as, then the desk ruling. Built as a pop-over under the gear in the bar, over the page, with the actor's username, full name, timezone and roles read from ~/.walkdown/config.yml and said so.
Record as is the username the records carry; the full name is only how you are shown. The design had one box.
The desk ruling — tilt, tip, depth, spacing, ink, hide — is as designed, with Reset.

start.title: first run
redlines: As designed: a first step, not an error. The build explains why a server is needed (a browser tab cannot read the filesystem) before naming walkdown serve; the design said it in one line.
The server box and Connect are the Blueprints tab's own row, drawn here too (n-0236).

project-modal.title: which project?
redlines: Built from the proposal that was promoted on 2026-09-10 (n-0271): the modal covers the whole chrome, panel included, and the board behind it is blurred.
The address is named, then what is true of it (no blueprint claims it), then the two commands — walkdown claims and walkdown import — then every project this machine has, with its blueprint count.
This one screen also answers several projects claim this page and no page to route from (ADR 0001 §7); the retired unclaimed-page drawing was one of the three it folded.

choose-blueprint.title: choose a blueprint
redlines: The gate itself only rises when a project holds several blueprints and none is picked; this machine holds one per project, so what is drawn is the Blueprints tab, which lists the same rows with the same anchors (start.folder, start.options).

The design asked which blueprint is this site? with radio marks and a description per row. Built: the server row above, the folder named, and each blueprint as a row with its description — the one the page claims first.
Nothing is remembered for the site (ADR 0001 §9); the address carries the pick instead.

rule-detail-setup.title: rule detail, the screen's setup steps are running
redlines: Drawn over the example's waitlist, as every as-built is: the steps sign a returning visitor in and join twice, where the design signs a manager in to an expense.

Setup sits directly under the statement and above Screen and Steps, where the built rule detail keeps what happens before the steps. The design had the feedback box and the verdict pair between the statement and Setup; the built detail puts those in the conversation, at the foot.
The target's name stands beside the App button on every bar once a blueprint declares two targets. This design drew the bar without it; the App pane's target picker drew it.
The progress card's line for a post reads Posting the form to and the path. The design said Posting the sign-in form to: the panel cannot know what a form is for.

app-setup-failed.title: a setup step failed, so the screen is not loaded
redlines: As drawn: the step, its path and what it got, then what was not loaded and what to do. The rows and the words are the design's.
Setup sits under the statement, above Screen and Steps, with the feedback box and the verdict pair at the foot in the conversation (see rule detail's redlines).
The App pane behind the card is the as-built's stand-in box. In the panel the card covers the frame, which is left on the step that failed.

screen-picker-tied.title: the address matches two screens that differ in setup
redlines: The note is the design's, word for word, with each state's setup in a sentence under its title.

The ordinary picker stays under the note: the List and Storyboard tabs, Detect from the page and every screen. The design drew the note alone. A person who is on neither state can still pick another screen.
Design and App are dimmed while the question stands, and the bar reads Which screen?, as drawn.

app-target-picker.title: the App pane's target picker
redlines: As drawn: the target's name against the App button, a row for each target that has a base URL with its address under it, a tick on the one in use, and the foot note.
A target with no base URL is not listed, and a blueprint with one target shows no picker at all. The design drew two targets and did not say.
The bar reads No screen here because the as-built frames the example's design page, not its app.

rule-detail-targets.title: rule detail, a verdict on each target
redlines: A row for each tier on each target that has a run, and what the check said under its row, as drawn.
Each row keeps the built detail's own shape: verdict, who, and how long ago on one line (pass · agent · 75d ago). The design set the time at the right edge as a clock time.
The check's file is given with its folder (spec/waitlist.spec.ts:27), as the ledger records it. The design showed the file name alone.
The first target keeps its row when it has no run, so never run is still said; any other target gets a row only once it has one.
Evidence sits after Steps, where the built rule detail has always had it. The design had it above them.

cli/serve-anywhere.title: walkdown serve, started outside any blueprint, serves them all
redlines: The command as typed carries --port 0, so the capture never collides with a serve already on 4700; the port it printed is shown as 4700, serve's own default.

The design's second half, the same command inside ~/shop with --blueprint checkout, is one screen per command here and is not drawn. Its lines, the (default) mark and A page that names no blueprint opens <id>., are checked by test/serve.test.js.
The design draws no exit code; a server stopped with Ctrl-C ends 130.

cli/lint-proposes-gone.title: Lint names a design request whose proposed version is gone
redlines: The command as typed carries --no-checks, where the design runs a bare walkdown lint. The fixture's one rule asks for checks that this throwaway project has none of, so a bare lint adds a [coverage] warning the design does not draw, and the closing line would read 1 warning where it says 0. With checks skipped, the two errors and the closing counts are the design's.

cli/hash-reword-adds-excuse.title: hash --reword refuses a rule that gained an excuse
redlines: The advice line gives walkdown hash --write --changed "<why>" <rules> where the design gives a plain walkdown hash --write <rules>. A plain write on a signed rule is refused since status.derived.a-change-says-why (2026-10-23), so the rule's step was reworded to name --changed; a text change, so the design was not redrawn.

mode-switch.title: the mode switcher, on Walkdown
redlines: Captured with the switcher's list open. The design shows the bar closed and the list as a small state beside it.
The bar keeps the project button between the switcher and the blueprint's name, as it was before the switcher. The design drew the blueprint's name alone.

The fade is still centred over the bar and not in the row, as the design drew it for a narrow window. On a screen with two design versions the screen picker's title is cut shorter to make room for the switcher.

mode-boards.title: Boards, taking the whole window
redlines: The board is drawn as its phases and its cards in file order, each card with its story's title. Lanes, groups, hand-offs, marks and pictures wait for the board's own rules.
There is no Follow control: following a persona needs lanes.
Time runs Across and Down, the zoom buttons and Reset float at the bottom right as designed. Across and Down turn the phases from columns to rows.
The gear opens a pop-over that says Boards has no settings yet. The design's four settings were placeholders.
The bar keeps the project button, as on Walkdown.

mode-personas.title: Personas, taking the whole window
redlines: A card holds the persona's title, what they are a persona of, a line about them, what they use and their users. The avatar, the fixtures and targets of each user, the stories by mark and the boards wait for the personas' own rules.
Personas are listed in the storyboard's order, with no group headings and no key to the marks.
The line under the grid naming the systems is not drawn.
The gear opens a pop-over that says Personas has no settings yet.
